rows.ingredient_en: Antioxidants (vitamin C, vitamin E, and coenzyme Q10[CoQ10])
rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Minimize free-radical damage to skeletal muscle, thereby reducing muscle fatigue, inflammation, and soreness
rows.evidence_description_en: Several small clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: Do not directly improve performance; appear to hinder some physiological and physical exercise-induced adaptations
rows.safety_evidence_en: Safe at recommended intakes; some safety concerns reported with high doses
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Potential for diarrhea, nausea, abdominal cramps, and other gastrointestinal disturbances with vitamin C intakes of more than 2,000 mg/day in adults; increased risk of hemorrhagic effects with vitamin E intakes of more than 1,500 International Units (IU)/day (natural form) or 1,100 IU/day (synthetic form) in adults; nausea, heartburn, and other side effects with CoQ10

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Increases blood flow and delivery of oxygen and nutrients to skeletal muscle; serves as a substrate for creatine production; increases secretion of human growth hormone to stimulate muscle growth
rows.evidence_description_en: Limited clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Little to no effect on vasodilation, blood flow, or exercise metabolites; little evidence of increases in muscle creatine content
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for use of up to 9 g/day for weeks; adverse effects possible with larger doses
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Gastrointestinal effects, such as diarrhea and nausea

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Dilates blood vessels in exercising muscle, reduces oxygen use, and improves energy production
rows.evidence_description_en: Limited clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Might improve performance and endurance to some degree in time trials and time-to-exhaustion tests among runners, swimmers, rowers, and cyclists; appears to be most effective in recreationally active nonathletes
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for short-term use at commonly recommended amounts (approximately 2 cups)
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Increases synthesis of carnosine, a dipeptide that buffers changes in muscle pH, thereby reducing muscle fatigue and loss of force production; considerable individual variation in associated muscle carnosine synthesis
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Inconsistent effects on performance in competitive events requiring high-intensity effort over a short period, such as team sports; little or no performance benefit in activities lasting more than 10 minutes
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for use of 1.6–6.4 g/day for up to 8 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Paresthesia (tingling) in face, neck, back of hands, and upper trunk with at least 800 mg or more than 10 mg/kg body mass; pruritus (itchy skin)

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Helps stressed and damaged skeletal muscle cells restore their structure and function
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Might help speed up recovery from exercise of sufficient amount and intensity to induce skeletal muscle damage
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for typical dose of 3 g/day for up to 2 months
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Might increase creatine production, blood nitric oxide levels, or water retention in cells
rows.evidence_description_en: Limited clinical trials in men with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Potential but modest strength and power-based performance improvements in bodybuilders and cyclists
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for 2–5 g/day for up to 15 days
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.ingredient_en: Branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, and valine)
rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Can be metabolized by mitochondria in skeletal muscle to provide energy during exercise
rows.evidence_description_en: Limited number of short-term clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: Little evidence of improved performance in endurance-related aerobic events; possibility of greater gains in muscle mass and strength during training
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for 20 g/day or less for up to 6 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Blocks activity of the neuromodulator adenosine; reduces perceived pain and exertion
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous clinical trials with mostly consistent results
rows.research_findings_en: Might enhance performance in endurance-type activities (e.g., running) and intermittent, long-duration activities (e.g., soccer) when taken before activity
rows.safety_evidence_en: Reasonably safe at up to 400–500 mg/day for adults
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Insomnia, restlessness, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and arrhythmia; risk of death with acute oral dose of approximately 10–14 g pure caffeine (150–200 mg/kg)

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Dilates blood vessels to increase delivery of oxygen and nutrients to skeletal muscle
rows.evidence_description_en: Few clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Little research support for use to enhance performance
rows.safety_evidence_en: Few safety concerns reported for up to 9 g for 1 day or 6 g/day for up to 16 days
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Gastrointestinal discomfort

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Helps supply muscles with energy for short-term, predominantly anaerobic activity
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous clinical trials generally showing a benefit for high-intensity, intermittent activity; potential variation in individual responses
rows.research_findings_en: May increase strength, power, and work from maximal effort muscle contractions; over time helps body adapt to athlete-training regimens; of little value for endurance sports
rows.safety_evidence_en: Few safety concerns reported at typical dose (e.g., loading dose of 20 g/day for up to 7 days and 3–5 g/day for up to 12 weeks)
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Weight gain due to water retention; anecdotal reports of nausea, diarrhea, muscle cramps, muscle stiffness, heat intolerance

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Contains growth factors (such as insulin-like growth factor-1 [IGF-1]) that could promote muscle tissue growth
rows.evidence_description_en: Few short-term clinical trials that show no benefit for physical performance
rows.research_findings_en: No evidence for improving aerobic or anaerobic performance, muscular strength, or endurance
rows.safety_evidence_en: Safety not well studied
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Hypoglycemia, headache, edema, and joint pain (from prescription IGF-1); banned in professional athletic competition

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Steroid hormone that can be converted into testosterone and estradiol
rows.evidence_description_en: Small number of clinical trials that show no benefit for physical performance
rows.research_findings_en: No evidence of increases in strength, aerobic capacity, lean body mass, or testosterone levels in men
rows.safety_evidence_en: Safety not well studied; no safety concerns reported for up to 150 mg/day for 6–12 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Over several months, raises testosterone levels in women, which can cause acne and growth of facial hair

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Unknown mechanism of action; Panax ginseng used in traditional Chinese medicine as a tonic for stamina and vitality; Siberian ginseng used to reduce fatigue
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous small clinical trials, most showing no benefit for physical performance
rows.research_findings_en: In various doses and types of preparations, no effects on peak power output, time to exhaustion, perceived exertion, recovery from intense activity, oxygen consumption, or heart rate
rows.safety_evidence_en: Few safety concerns reported with short-term use
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: For Panax ginseng: headache, sleep disturbances, and gastrointestinal disorders; for Siberian ginseng: none known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Involved in metabolism and energy production; contributes nitrogen for many critical biochemical reactions
rows.evidence_description_en: Few studies of use to enhance performance directly
rows.research_findings_en: In adult weightlifters, no effect on muscle performance, body composition, or muscle-protein degradation; may help with recovery of muscle strength and reduce muscle soreness after exercise
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported with about 45 g/day for 6 weeks; safe use of up to 0.42 g/kg body weight (e.g., 30 g/day in a person weighing 154 lb) by many patients with serious conditions (e.g., infections, intestinal diseases, and burns)
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Increases oxygen uptake, reduces heart rate, and decreases lactate concentrations during exercise
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Improved work capacity with correction of iron deficiency anemia; conflicting evidence on whether milder iron deficiency without anemia impairs exercise performance
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for use at recommended intakes (8 mg/day for healthy men and postmenopausal women and 18 mg/day for healthy premenopausal women)
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Gastric upset, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and fainting at intakes above 45 mg/day

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Builds, maintains, and repairs muscle
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: Optimizes muscle training response during exercise and subsequent recovery period
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported at daily recommended intakes for athletes of up to about 2.0 g/kg body weight (e.g., 136 g for a person weighing 150 lb)
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Increases mitochondria in muscle, reduces oxidative stress, decreases inflammation, and improves blood flow
rows.evidence_description_en: Numerous small, short-term clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: Little to no effect on endurance performance or maximal oxygen consumption
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for 1,000 mg/day or less for up to 8 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Involved in production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
rows.evidence_description_en: A few small, short-term, clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: Little to no effect on exercise capacity in both trained and untrained adults
rows.safety_evidence_en: Safety as a dietary supplement not well studied; no safety concerns reported for up to 10 g/day for 8 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Enhances disposal of hydrogen ions generated from intense muscle activity, thereby reducing metabolic acidosis and resulting fatigue
rows.evidence_description_en: Many small, short-term clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: Might provide minor to moderate performance benefit for short-term and intermittent high-intensity activity, especially in trained athletes
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for short-term use of up to 300 mg/kg body weight
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: Nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, and vomiting

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Phytochemicals in tart cherries may facilitate exercise recovery by reducing pain and inflammation
rows.evidence_description_en: A few clinical trials with conflicting results
rows.research_findings_en: Variable results for aiding muscle strength recovery, reducing soreness, or reducing inflammatory effects on lungs after exercise; insufficient research on ability to improve aerobic performance
rows.safety_evidence_en: No safety concerns reported for about 1/2 quart of juice or 480 mg freeze-dried Montmorency tart-cherry-skin powder per day for up to 2 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: None known

rows.proposed_mechanism_en: Increases serum testosterone and luteinizing hormone concentrations, thereby promoting skeletal muscle hypertrophy
rows.evidence_description_en: A few small, short-term clinical trials
rows.research_findings_en: No effect on strength, lean body mass, or sex hormone levels
rows.safety_evidence_en: Safety not well studied; no safety concerns reported at up to 3.21 mg/kg/day for 8 weeks
rows.reported_adverse_effects_en: One case report of harm from product labeled but not confirmed to contain Tribulus terrestris

footnotes: * References to support statements in Table 1 are provided in subsequent text.

** The evidence of efficacy and safety is for the individual ingredients. The efficacy and safety of these ingredients might be different when they are combined with other ingredients in a product or training plan.
